en: The Five Verses on the Loincloth (by Śaṅkarācārya)
Always delighting in the statements of Vedānta, they possess only a loincloth as their five-fold requirements and find contentment with mere alms-food.
Wandering within their hearts free from sorrow, clad only in a loincloth, they are indeed fortunate. ||1||
Relying solely on the root of the tree,
consulting with their two hands as to how to eat, they treated even prosperity with contempt, as if it were a mere ragged garment.
Truly, those who possess a loincloth are fortunate. ||2||
Contented in the state of their own bliss,
with the activities of all their senses perfectly stilled,
they delight day and night in the happiness of Brahman.
Indeed, those who possess a loincloth are truly fortunate. ||3||
Transforming their state from that of the body and so forth,
beholding their own Self within the self,
they remember neither end, nor middle, nor outside.
Truly, those who possess a loincloth are fortunate. ||4||
Uttering the purifying syllable of Brahman,
contemplating "I am Brahman," they wander through the quarters as mendicants subsisting on alms.
Truly, those who possess a loincloth are fortunate. ||5||
Thus ends the *Kaupīnapañcaka* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
